title: Electrical engineering
blurb: How electrical plant behaves, ashore and afloat: AC circuits, machines, power at sea, control and fault-finding, each course built in full before you open it.

folders.title: Electrical principles
folders.blurb: The behaviour of AC circuits and the machines built on it, in principles that hold on any installation.

courses.title: AC circuits
courses.blurb: From the turning coil to three-phase power: rms, reactance, impedance, power factor and its correction, star and delta.

courses.title: Transformers
courses.blurb: Turns ratios, losses, efficiency and regulation, and three-phase transformer connections.

folders.title: Power and machines at sea
folders.blurb: Generation, distribution, motors and drives, and the instruments that watch over them.

courses.title: Motors
courses.blurb: What you need to know on each motor: how it works, how it behaves, where it is used, how it fails, and the starter and drive that control it.

courses.title: Three-phase power systems at sea
courses.blurb: Generators, their speed and excitation, running in parallel, insulated and earthed neutrals, and earth fault detection.

courses.title: Instrumentation and control
courses.blurb: Sensors, transducers and control loops on the plant.

courses.title: HV Subsea Cable Testing
courses.blurb: Your subsea cable testing course taught back to you: make the cable safe, then DLRO, IR and PI, sheath, VLF, TDR and LIRA on one 66 kV wind farm cable, until the fault is found.

courses.title: Maintenance and fault-finding
courses.blurb: Systematic fault-finding, insulation resistance and condition monitoring.

folders.title: Installation design (BS 7671)
folders.blurb: Designing and verifying installations ashore to BS 7671, built to your Level 4 course.

courses.title: Design and verification, a Level 4 refresher
courses.blurb: Your Level 4 course taught back to you: recall first, the why where you need it, then practice in the City & Guilds shapes on your own showroom assignment.
